why: Lowers by $16,000 reverses the sign; raises by $120,000 ignores the tiered price and drops the $1.00 per-shake cost as if it cancelled (360k × $2 − 300k × $2); lowers by $120,000 applies $2.40 to every shake and forgets the 20% volume rise (300k × 40c); no common slip lands on +$16,000.

The profit statement reads Spokewise's higher margin as more profit, the maintenance statement reads Velora's higher percentage as a larger amount, and the fare statement is the single statement without basis that sourceHas allows.

2% takes the loss as a share of sales to be the rise needed, 22% takes the increase as a share of the new sales instead of the old ($149m ÷ $669m), and 9% (the operating-cost share) is at worst the one numeric filler below the answer that sourceHas allows; no slip lands on 29%.

The (1 − rate) formula confuses the salesperson's cut with the part the dealership keeps; the formula that adds count and price also swaps the rates (two slips); the one that divides by the rates also multiplies by hours (two slips).
$5.5 million forgets to split the 250,000 customers into quintiles, $2.9 million gives the new total profit (58.5 × 50,000) instead of the increase, and $14.6 million makes both slips together.

1.4 applies the gap in the two shares (77.1 points) to Hospital 1's 1.8% growth (or gives Hospital 10's figure alone), and 0.2 and 1.0 continue the even 0.4 spacing of that grid; no slip lands on 0.6 (capping Hospital 1 at 100% gives 0.4).

55% applies the second pie to all respondents rather than to the 70% (wrong base), 70% reads 'main reason' as 'only reason' (over-reading), and the spending statement is the single statement without basis that sourceHas allows.

5.0 is the total fall over three years left unaveraged, 0.2 reads the fruit juice lines and averages over four years (two slips), and 0.6 is the single numeric filler sourceHas allows, roughly continuing the threefold spacing; the slips that still give 1.6 are the ones sourceHas names.

Twice compares margins alone (15% ÷ 8%) or revenues alone; the same swaps the two margin lines (road at 8%, children's at 15%); half compares margins alone and the wrong way round (two slips); skipping the growth step still gives three times, but sourceHas names that slip.

1.3 applies the gap in the two shares (83.4 points) to Territory A's 1.5% growth (1.25), and 0.1 and 0.9 continue the even 0.4 spacing of that grid; no slip lands on 0.5 (capping Territory A at 100% gives 0.3).
